```markdown
# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made:
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), in the existing uv workspace of four packages.
- Platform per the ADR (Proposed, 2026-10-05). Accepting it is a precondition of Stage 7, not of earlier stages.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes downloaded for a chosen quarter range | §3 R1; §2.1; §4.2 | A | 1 | Measured by Stage 1 (bytes, time, peak memory for one quarter). Full-range cost ≈ that figure × quarters in `backfill.*` |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2; §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year plus listing reads, at the 3 req/s target (§4.8); per-file size measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet built from the ingested indexes | §3 R3; §4.4; §4.5; §4.6 | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1 (parse and write time and rows for one quarter) |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure, with logs and alerts | §3 R4; §4.1; §4.7; §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend not estimable before deployment; measured by the Stage 7 smoke test (§7 step 4) |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | None material |
| O6 | ETL re-run from stored original bytes, with no new download | §3 R6; §4.3; §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage ≈ raw bytes retained per snapshot; per-quarter bytes measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of quarterly indexes against the catalog | §3 R7; §4.2; §4.4 | A | 7 | Weekly re-read of every supported quarter: Stage 1's per-quarter bytes × range, under the 3 req/s target |
| O8 | All SEC traffic under one request budget, however many workers run | §3 R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | None material |
| O9 | Readers finding current data through one versioned pointer per quarter | §3 R9; §4.5; §4.6 | A | 9 | None material |
| O10 | Records leaving the catalog only by explicit, hash-bound approval | §3 R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Your time per gated closed-quarter candidate; frequency measured once Stage 6 runs on real data |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and rate target held as reviewed configuration | §3 R11; §4.8 | A | 11 | None material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Core — one real quarter to Parquet
      Objective: Download one archived quarter's master index from the SEC and parse it into canonical Parquet rows, run locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing (generated package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a working downloader and parser for quarterly master indexes, emitting the §4.5 row contract; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one real archived quarter's index fetched with an identifying User-Agent, at or below 3 req/s, with SHA-256 and byte count recorded. O3 — a Parquet file of that quarter whose rows meet the §4.5 row contract, with malformed rows refused and reported, not dropped. The findings file records bytes downloaded, request count, elapsed time, peak memory and row count for the real run.
      Leaves out: source manifest and content-addressed raw store → Stage 3; generations and active pointer → Stage 4; shared request lease, retry policy and typed configuration → Stage 5; golden fixtures across the full backfill range and §6 full validation suite → Stage 7; Azure deployment → Stage 7; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from a handoff date, through the same downloader and parser as Stage 1.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader and parser
      Produces: discovery via `index.json` listings for full-index and daily-index; daily and quarterly observations merged on the §4.4 key; a backfill command and a daily command over shared code
      Exit: O2 — real daily indexes from a chosen handoff date through the present are ingested and deduplicated against the baseline quarter, and a fixture of a missed run across a quarter boundary catches up without skipping a file or advancing past a failed listing. O5 — backfill and daily commands call the same downloader and parser modules, with no source-specific copy.
      Leaves out: source manifest → Stage 3; publication pointer → Stage 4; shared request lease → Stage 5; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Raw snapshots, source manifest and replay
      Objective: Keep original bytes content-addressed and track source, snapshot and processing state, so ETL replays from storage.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 2's discovery, collection and parsing
      Produces: the §4.5 raw and observation paths; the §4.5 source-manifest records; processing transitions; per-source-file checkpoints and immutable worksets (§4.1, §4.2)
      Exit: O6 — with SEC access disabled, a parser-version change rebuilds observations from stored raw bytes, a repeated run over unchanged hashes and versions is a no-op, and a run interrupted after some members resumes without redoing them.
      Leaves out: generations and active pointer → Stage 4; shared request lease → Stage 5; Azure storage backends → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as a complete, immutable generation that readers reach only through a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3's observations and source manifest
      Produces: the §4.5 curated generation layout, manifest.json and changes.parquet; the §4.6 publish steps; a reader path that resolves the pointer
      Exit: O9 — readers of a real quarter resolve the active pointer to a manifest file list. Injected crashes before files finish, before the pointer update and just after it leave readers seeing only complete generations. Two competing publishers cannot lose an update.
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Table Storage backend → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: One request budget and validated configuration
      Objective: Put every SEC request behind one shared lease and rate budget, with retry and error policy from validated configuration.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 2's collector; Stage 3's attempt records
      Produces: the §4.3 shared lease and throttle; the §4.8 HTTP retry, timeout and Retry-After policy; the §5 access outcomes; typed configuration validated before I/O
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill and daily collectors under test issue no overlapping requests, retries count toward the budget, lease loss stops new requests, and a 403 halts the run. O11 — every §4.8 key loads from configuration, and each §5 configuration error is refused before any network request.
      Leaves out: Storage-backed lease on Azure → Stage 7; reconciliation as a budget consumer → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and gate closed-quarter withdrawals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4's publication; Stage 5's request budget; Stage 2's shared commands
      Produces: a reconciliation command over the shared code; §4.4 open- and closed-quarter precedence; approval records; the `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7 — a reconciliation run over real quarters skips unchanged hashes and records additions and field updates in changes.parquet. O10 — on corrected fixtures, open-quarter absence withdraws nothing, closed-quarter removal stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval naming that source hash, a reused approval is refused, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key.
      Leaves out: weekly schedule → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment and full validation
      Objective: Run the shared worker on Azure in an isolated environment, with production triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; the ADR and spec accepted, with the §7 step 1 settings recorded
      Produces: ADF pipelines, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS and Table Storage backends, managed identities, logs and alerts under `infra/`; the §6 CI suite and integration tests; golden fixtures for the chosen backfill range
      Exit: O4 — in the isolated environment, the §7 step 4 smoke test against one archived quarter and one published daily index records byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate. The step 5 replay with SEC access disabled shows unchanged logical output. Every §6 CI exit criterion passes.
      Leaves out: production triggers, full backfill and runbooks → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the full backfill, catch daily ingestion up, and enable the daily and weekly triggers on reviewed versions.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (full range, on schedule)
      Consumes: Stage 7's deployed environment and smoke-test record
      Produces: the published baseline; enabled triggers; §8 runbooks and README; a release record
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline quarter is published, or the incomplete range is approved and recorded. O2 — the daily trigger is enabled after the catch-up result is accepted, and later scheduled runs show in durable reports. O7 — after one manual reconciliation with gated candidates resolved, the weekly trigger runs and its report is recorded. The release record names image digest, configuration revision and active generations.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric (derive-roadmap §6) over O1–O11. Each verdict needs a path:line or test name and the stage plan that built it; a stamp alone is not evidence. Every §3 requirement is cited by an outcome, so no extra spec rows apply. An unmet outcome exits as a new stage, or as a written deferral.
```

**Message:** I wrote the roadmap: eight stages over O1–O11, and their order diverges from your ranking on purpose. It goes by dependency: a local core run on one real quarter comes first, then daily ingestion, replay, publication and the request budget, all before reconciliation needs them. Azure deployment (O4) waits until the code it deploys exists. Do you approve this partition, so I commit it and hand Stage 1 to brainstorming?
